b1-40-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Dreams and Support
b1-40-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you dream about and who you can count on. You dream of travelling to South Africa to see your family, and you can count on your sister Lauren.
b1-40-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you dream of and who you can count on.
cues: Say what you dream of doing
Say who you can count on
b1-40-01.target: Sueño con viajar a Sudáfrica y sé que puedo contar con mi hermana Lauren.
b1-40-01.english: I dream of travelling to South Africa and I know I can count on my sister Lauren.
b1-40-01.canDo: I can use verbs with a fixed preposition such as soñar con, pensar en, contar con and depender de.

b1-40-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Party, but Home
b1-40-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you went to the party at your office last night. You did not go to the party: you stayed at home and studied Spanish.
b1-40-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you did not go to the party, and say what you did instead.
cues: Say you did not go to the party
b1-40-02.target: No fui a la fiesta, sino que me quedé en casa estudiando español.
b1-40-02.english: I didn't go to the party, but stayed at home studying Spanish.
b1-40-02.canDo: I can choose between pero, sino and sino que.

b1-40-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Photography Course
b1-40-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you thought of your photography course. You liked the walks around the city best, and the difficult part was getting up early.
b1-40-03.prompt: Tell Carlos the best thing and the difficult part of the course.
cues: Say the best thing about the course
b1-40-03.target: Lo mejor fueron los paseos por la ciudad y lo difícil fue levantarse temprano.
b1-40-03.english: The best thing was the walks around the city and the difficult part was getting up early.
b1-40-03.canDo: I can use lo + adjective, as in lo importante, lo bueno and lo difícil.

b1-40-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Long Meeting
b1-40-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the long meeting at your office went. It was very difficult and you finished very tired.
b1-40-04.prompt: Tell Meg how difficult the meeting was and how tired you were.
cues: Say how difficult the meeting was
b1-40-04.target: No sabes lo difícil que fue la reunión y lo cansado que terminé.
b1-40-04.english: You don't know how difficult the meeting was and how tired I was at the end.
b1-40-04.canDo: I can say how difficult, fast or good something is, with lo + adjective + que.

b1-40-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Weekend
b1-40-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you are going to the cinema on Saturday. You are not going to the cinema: you are staying at home, and you are thinking about how well you are going to rest.
b1-40-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you are not doing, what you are doing instead and what you are thinking about.
cues: Say you are not going to the cinema
Say you are staying at home
Say what you are thinking about
b1-40-05.target: No voy al cine, sino que me quedo en casa. Pienso en lo bien que voy a descansar.
b1-40-05.english: I'm not going to the cinema; I'm staying at home. I'm thinking about how well I'm going to rest.
b1-40-05.canDo: I can combine fixed prepositions, sino (que) and lo in one text.

b1-40-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Summer
b1-40-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you dream about for the summer. You do not dream of a long trip but of a quiet week at home. The important thing is to rest, and you count on Meg.
b1-40-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you dream of, what is important and who you count on.
cues: Say what you dream of, and what you don't
Say what the important thing is
b1-40-consolidation.target: No sueño con un viaje largo, sino con una semana tranquila en casa. Lo importante es descansar, y cuento contigo.
b1-40-consolidation.english: I don't dream of a long trip but of a quiet week at home. The important thing is to rest, and I count on you.
b1-40-consolidation.canDo: I can use verbs with fixed prepositions, sino (que) and lo + adjective.
